findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === is always false
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable the code does `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` to detect a zero-length/unavailable date override. These are two distinct Dayjs objects, so === is always false. As a result a full-day block override is never recognized and slots on a day the fixed host marked unavailable will still be returned as available, allowing booking when no fixed host is free.

findings.title: Working-hours check ignores event length
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime.hour()*60+slotStartTime.minute()`. The slot end (start + eventLength) is never used, so a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after workingHours.endTime is treated as available. This re-introduces bookable slots past the end of availability for fixed/loose host filtering.

findings.title: Working-hours exclusion uses ANY instead of ALL logic
findings.body: The code does `workingHours.find(wh => slot outside wh)` and returns unavailable if any entry matches. With split working hours, multiple intervals, or aggregated collective hours, a slot inside one valid interval is still outside another interval, so find succeeds and the slot is wrongly rejected. The correct check is that the slot is inside at least one applicable interval; otherwise valid fixed-host slots disappear.

findings.title: Date-override timezone shift drops day overflow
findings.body: Overrides are converted to `hour()*60+minute` after applying the organizer-to-invitee offset, discarding the date. If the offset pushes the override past midnight, the minutes wrap (e.g. 23:30 + 60min becomes 00:30) but are still applied to the original invitee day, and the activeOverrides filter only tests the override start instant against the invitee day. Overrides near midnight or with large organizer/invitee offsets are therefore applied to the wrong day or truncated.

findings.title: Date-override day/range comparison mixes shifted and unshifted times
findings.body: checkIfIsAvailable computes `utcOffset = dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` then compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset).format('YYYY MM DD')` to `slotStartTime.format('YYYY MM DD')` where slotStartTime is UTC. Shifting the override instant by the negated offset before comparing to an unshifted UTC slot corrupts both the day match and the start/end range checks whenever the organizer timezone is not UTC, so overrides are matched to the wrong day or judged with wrong boundaries.
